pages.title: Forest of Magic
pages.text: A dense overworld biome of towering blue firs and giant mushrooms: Ghost Fire, Dream, and Demonic Miasma. Entering it earns you this guide. Watch the haze between the great caps: some of it bites.

Giant firs and mushroom trees crowd around clearings, ponds, and mushroom glades, with the oldest and tallest standing over everything else. The forest floor is never bare: grass, ferns, and flowers run right underneath the giant crowns.

pages.title: Ghost Fire Mushrooms
pages.text: The mushrooms that light the forest floor. Every cap gives off a faint glow of its own, so a patch of them reads like a row of lanterns strung under the canopy, and a mature ghost fire stands taller than a person on a slender stem.

pages.title: Dream Mushrooms
pages.text: The tallest and roundest of the three, and entirely lightless. Dream mushrooms give off no glow whatsoever, so a dream grove stays dim even at midday — which is how you learn to recognise one from a distance.

pages.title: Demonic Miasma Mushrooms
pages.text: The red ones. They breathe out a heavy haze that pools beneath their caps and creeps along the forest floor, and standing in it is genuinely bad for you — the air itself seems to fight back. Everything about them is a warning, down to the colour.

pages.title: Blue Fir
pages.text: The reason the forest has a canopy at all. Tall straight trunks under long, flat tiers of needles, where most trees carry a rounded crown. The oldest of them stand far above everything else in Gensokyo.

pages.title: Trunks and Branches
pages.text: What grows on the trees rather than under them. Eugune are small bracket mushrooms that stick out sideways from bark and logs, and there are three kinds: a red one, a brown one, and a glowing one. Evergreen vines hang from the branches in long strands, deepest in the oldest stands.

pages.title: Forest Floor
pages.text: The undergrowth. Star flowers, tall enough to be noticed and bright enough to be worth the detour; flame cattails standing in and around the ponds; broom grass in the drifts; and bracken threading through all of it. This is what makes the floor of the Magical Forest feel like a garden nobody planted.
